function: Learned joint task offloading portions and bandwidth allocation on ground-to-UAV and UAV-to-satellite links to maximize reliably offloaded tasks; bandwidth allocation is the physical-layer part (pp. 3, 6).
system: 3-6 relay UAVs, 15-24 single-antenna ground users, one satellite edge server at 780 km; FDMA; carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 4, 9-10).
method: DDPG actor-critic (single agent) and cluster-based CMADDPG, one agent per UAV with centralized critics and decentralized actors; reinforcement learning, CTDE (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: Custom Python simulation: shadowed-Rician space-to-air channel and Rician LoS air-to-ground channel with path-loss exponent 2, from refs [28], [12]; no standardized channel model or measured data (pp. 4, 9).
test_conditions: Training curves shown per scenario (N=15, 21, 24 users; M=3, 4, 6 UAVs); Figs. 7-8 sweep bandwidth budget and CPU demand; no unseen-condition test or adaptation stated (pp. 9-11).
baselines: Non-learned only: equal bandwidth allocation (Fig. 7), Equal-Split and Random (Fig. 8); no earlier learned method or standard learned algorithm is compared (p. 11).
metrics: Episode reward (training convergence), average reliable task offloading portion, average per-GU latency (pp. 9-11).
complexity: Orders O(B(F_actor+F_critic)) per DDPG update and O(B*M*(F_actor+F*_critic)) for MADDPG, plus memory order; no FLOPs, parameter counts, or runtime reported (p. 8).
openness: none; Python with existing packages (pytorch, gymnasium, pettingzoo), no link to the authors' code or data (p. 9).
q1_support: p. 4: "adopt the shadowed-Rician fading (SRF) model to describe the" space-to-air channel, plus Rician fading for air-to-ground; parameters in Table II (p. 9). Custom statistical models; no 3GPP TR 38.811 or 38.901 model, public ray-tracing dataset, or measured data is cited.
q2_support: p. 10: "Training Performance With Varying of Number of UAV" Agents (Fig. 6); Figs. 3-5 also show training per scenario, and Figs. 7-8 (p. 11) sweep bandwidth budget and CPU demand. The paper never states that a trained model is tested in an unseen scenario or adapted to one.
q3_support: p. 11: "1) Equal-Split and 2) Random" and the Fig. 7 caption "equal bandwidth allocation scheme": non-learned baselines only. No earlier learned method or standard learned algorithm is compared, and Algorithm 1 (DDPG) and Algorithm 2 (CMADDPG), both the paper's own, are never compared with each other.
q4_support: p. 8: "using a mini-batch of size B, the time complexity" is O(B(F_actor + F_critic)) for DDPG and O(B M (F_actor + F*_critic)) for MADDPG, with the memory order, in Section IV-C.
q5_support: p. 9: "in a Python environment, utilizing well-known packages," (pytorch, gymnasium, pettingzoo). Existing packages only; no link or availability statement for the authors' code or data, and the channels are synthetic.
notes: Borderline eligibility: the objective is reliable task offloading (above PHY), but the policy also learns bandwidth allocation on ground-to-UAV and UAV-to-satellite links (p. 6, Eq. 13), counted as physical-layer resource allocation in satellite and aerial links learned jointly with an above-PHY decision; included as area 6. All devices are single-antenna (p. 4), which NTN works admit. Channel parameters come from refs [28], [12], not from a standard. Single-agent DDPG (Algorithm 1) and multiagent CMADDPG (Algorithm 2) are both the paper's methods. Table II and Figs. 3 to 8 were read as images.
